title: Child Mortality Indicators: IMR, NMR, Perinatal Mortality, and Low Birth Weight

steps.title: Infant mortality rate defined
steps.tx: The **infant mortality rate** counts deaths in the first year of life per one thousand live births in the same year, and it is the most sensitive single indicator of health services and living conditions. India's rate fell from one hundred forty six in 1951 to twenty eight in 2020. Roughly two thirds of infant deaths now occur in the neonatal period itself.
steps.say: Infant mortality rate is deaths under one year per thousand live births. India brought it down to twenty eight, and most deaths now happen in the first month.

steps.tx: The **infant mortality rate** is deaths in the first year per one thousand live births in that year, and it is the single most sensitive indicator of health services and living conditions. India fell from one hundred forty six in 1951 to twenty eight in 2020. About two thirds of those infant deaths now occur in the neonatal period. A special newborn care unit exists because the rate is now largely a story of the first month, not of the later months of infancy.
steps.say: Infant mortality counts deaths before the first birthday per thousand live births. India reached twenty eight by 2020, down from one hundred forty six in 1951, and about two thirds of the deaths are now neonatal.

steps.title: Neonatal and perinatal mortality
steps.tx: Deaths in the first twenty eight days form the **neonatal mortality rate**, about twenty per one thousand live births in India, driven by prematurity, birth asphyxia, and sepsis. The perinatal mortality rate widens the lens to stillbirths after twenty eight weeks plus deaths in the first week, per one thousand total births, and it reflects the quality of antenatal and intranatal care most directly.
steps.say: Neonatal deaths cluster in the first week, from prematurity, asphyxia, and sepsis. Perinatal mortality adds stillbirths, so it judges pregnancy and labour care together.

steps.title: Under five mortality and child death rate
steps.tx: The **under five mortality rate** gives the probability of dying before the fifth birthday per one thousand live births; India recorded thirty two in 2020. It anchors the Sustainable Development Goal target of twenty five by 2030. The child mortality rate in demography instead counts deaths between exact ages one and five years among children alive at age one, a different denominator that examiners love to swap.
steps.say: Under five mortality is the chance of dying before age five per thousand live births. Do not confuse it with the one to four year child death rate.

steps.title: Low birth weight and its burden
steps.tx: A newborn under two thousand five hundred grams is **low birth weight**, whether preterm or growth restricted, and about one fifth of Indian newborns fall in this group. Low birth weight babies face hypothermia, hypoglycaemia, infection, and feeding failure, and they contribute the largest share of neonatal deaths. Maternal anaemia, short stature, young age, and closely spaced pregnancies are the upstream drivers.
steps.say: One in five Indian babies weighs under two thousand five hundred grams. These babies die more often from cold, low sugar, infection, and poor feeding.

rows: Weight below tenth percentile for gestation

steps.tx: Any newborn under two thousand five hundred grams is **low birth weight**, whether born early or growth restricted in utero, and about one fifth of Indian newborns are in this group. They are prone to hypothermia, hypoglycaemia, infection, and feeding failure, and they account for the largest share of neonatal deaths. Maternal anaemia, short stature, young age, and pregnancies spaced too closely drive the problem upstream of the scale reading.
steps.say: About one in five Indian newborns weighs under two thousand five hundred grams. They die more often from cold, low blood sugar, infection, and poor feeding, often after maternal anaemia, short stature, young age, or closely spaced pregnancies.

steps.title: Causes of neonatal and infant death
steps.tx: Prematurity complications, intrapartum asphyxia, and sepsis together cause most neonatal deaths, while pneumonia and diarrhoea dominate after the first month as **causes of infant mortality in India**. Congenital anomalies, neonatal tetanus, and severe malnutrition fill the remainder. Because causes differ by week of life, the remedy also changes: resuscitation and thermal care early, then immunisation, nutrition, and prompt case management.
steps.say: Early deaths come from prematurity, asphyxia, and sepsis. Later infant deaths come mainly from pneumonia and diarrhoea, so prevention must match the age.

steps.title: Social and biological determinants
steps.tx: Infant deaths concentrate where mothers are illiterate, deliveries happen at home, water is unsafe, and birth intervals are short; this pattern is called the **social determinants of infant mortality**. Biological factors include maternal age at both extremes, parity above four, and multiple pregnancy. Female infants receive care later in many households, which shows up as excess female mortality in the postneonatal months.
steps.say: Poverty, illiteracy, home delivery, and short birth gaps push infant mortality up. Care seeking is also slower for girls, which raises their later infancy deaths.

steps.title: Newborn care units: SNCU and NBSU
steps.tx: Sick newborns are stabilised close to home in a graded network where the **newborn stabilisation unit** at block level manages warmth, oxygen, and first dose antibiotics before referral, and the special newborn care unit at district level provides assisted ventilation and exchange transfusion. The newborn baby care corner in every labour room handles resuscitation in the first golden minute after birth.
steps.say: Block level stabilisation units keep a sick newborn warm and start treatment. District special newborn care units then provide ventilation and intensive care.

steps.title: Home based newborn care
steps.tx: Most newborn deaths happen at home in the first week, so the accredited social health activist completes scheduled **home based newborn care** visits on days one, three, seven, fourteen, twenty one, twenty eight, and forty two after a home delivery, with extra visits for low birth weight babies. She weighs the baby, checks temperature, cord, feeding, and danger signs, and refers at once for poor sucking, fast breathing, fever, or hypothermia.
steps.say: The ASHA visits every home born baby seven times in six weeks. Extra visits go to small babies, and any danger sign means immediate referral.

steps.title: Child survival interventions that work
steps.tx: The steepest mortality falls come from a short list of **child survival interventions**: skilled delivery with resuscitation, exclusive breastfeeding, complete immunisation, oral rehydration with zinc, pneumonia case management, vitamin A, and insecticide treated nets where malaria is endemic. Tracking every indicator through the Sample Registration System and the National Family Health Survey tells managers which district lags and why.
steps.say: Skilled delivery, breastfeeding, vaccines, oral rehydration with zinc, and pneumonia treatment save the most child lives. Surveys then show where the gaps remain.
